sense: look good on someone; be fitting for

terms.grammar: verb, second conjugation, impersonal: the thing as subject, the person in the accusative
evidence: Plaut. Most. 1.3.16: ut haec mē decet (Lewis & Short)
Prop. 4.4.53: tē toga picta decet (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Of clothes, colours and looks as of conduct: what becomes a person. Its everyday sense is the moral one, “it is proper, one ought” (nōn decet, it isn’t done); Cicero defines it as what is apt to the time and the person (Or. 74, Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: fit, suit (a person, an age, an occasion)
terms.grammar: verb, fourth conjugation, intransitive: the thing as subject, the person in the dative; often impersonal, convenit
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “it is fit, becoming, suitable”. The verb’s first sense is “come together, meet”; impersonally convenit is also “it is agreed”.

phrases.latin: quīn mē aspice et contemplā, ut haec mē decet
phrases.english: go on, look at me and see how well this suits me
small things suit a small man

phrases.latin: īte procul, juvenēs: mītis mihi convenit aetās: folle decet puerōs lūdere, folle senēs
phrases.english: off you go, young men: a gentle age suits me; it suits boys to play with the soft ball, and old men too
